title: Commas in lists
keyIdea: When a sentence lists three or more things, put a comma after each item to separate it from the next, and use "and" (or "or") before the last item: I bought apples, pears, plums and grapes. A comma goes after a whole item, so "chocolate cake" stays one thing. A list of two things just needs "and", with no comma.

kid: A list in a sentence names three or more things. Read this: I bought apples pears plums and grapes. It runs together. Where does one thing end and the next begin?
Commas fix it. Put a comma after each item, then use "and" before the last one. I bought apples, pears, plums and grapes. Now the reader sees four things.

Some items take two or more words, like chocolate cake or a red pen. The comma goes after the whole item, never in the middle. We packed sandwiches, chocolate cake and orange juice. That is three things, not four.
Two things do not need a comma. Write cats and dogs, not cats, and dogs. Also, never put a comma before the first item, straight after "and", or after the last item.
adult: This is a punctuation objective in the English national curriculum. Year 2 pupils learn to use commas to separate items in a list (English Appendix 2). They apply it in later years when writing and editing. In the US, Common Core L.1.2c asks first graders to use commas to separate single words in a series. L.5.2a extends this to punctuation that separates items in a series.

Key terms: a list (or series) is three or more items, joined by the conjunction and or or before the last one. Each item can be a single word or a noun phrase, such as a big red bus. The list comma separates the items. A comma before the final and is the serial or Oxford comma. Many UK schools leave it out, and many US style guides use it. Both are correct; teach children to be consistent.

Common mistakes: a comma after every word, which splits noun phrases like chocolate cake. A comma before the list starts (I bought, apples). A comma straight after and. A comma after the last item, before the verb (Red, blue and green, are colours). A comma in a list of only two things. Another slip is using commas but leaving out the final and, which makes the list seem unfinished.

In the lab, children tap gaps to add commas and watch a panel show how many things a reader would see. They keep two-word items whole and take the comma out of a list of two. They pack a lunch box sentence and choose comma or and for each join. Finally, they fix three lists with one slip each.

visual.caption: Is the list punctuated correctly? Drag each sentence, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: I need pens, pencils and paper.
I need, pens, pencils and paper.
We saw a fox, a deer and an owl.
We saw a fox, and a deer.
Tea, coffee, juice and milk are drinks.
Tea, coffee, and, milk are drinks.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: tap gaps to add list commas and see how many things the reader sees, pack a lunch box list, and fix three broken lists.

practice.prompt: Commas in lists: which sentence is punctuated correctly?
choices: We need eggs, flour and milk.
We need, eggs flour and milk.
We need eggs flour, and, milk.
practice.hint: Put a comma after each item except the last two, which "and" joins. No comma before the list starts.
practice.explain: We need eggs, flour and milk. One comma separates eggs from flour, and "and" joins the last two items.

practice.prompt: A list has {n} items, written without the serial comma (no comma before "and"). How many list commas does it need?
practice.hint: Every item gets a comma after it, except the last one and the one just before "and".
practice.explain: {n} items need {=n-2} commas: one after each item apart from the last two, which "and" joins.

practice.prompt: Which list keeps every item whole?
choices: I packed a sun hat, a towel and sun cream.
I packed a sun, hat, a towel and sun, cream.
I packed a, sun hat a towel, and sun cream.
practice.hint: "A sun hat" and "sun cream" are each one thing. Commas go after whole items.
practice.explain: A comma never splits an item. "A sun hat", "a towel" and "sun cream" are three things, so the list needs one comma and one "and".

practice.prompt: You use the serial (Oxford) comma, so there is also a comma before "and". How many commas does a list of {n} items need?
practice.hint: With the serial comma, every item except the last one has a comma after it.
practice.explain: {n} items with the serial comma need {=n-1} commas: one after every item except the last.

pool.prompt: How many things does this list name? We ate fish and chips, peas and ice cream.
pool.hint: Fish and chips is one meal. Count what the commas and the final "and" separate.
pool.explain: Fish and chips, peas, and ice cream: three things. The comma shows that fish and chips belongs together.

pool.prompt: Which sentence needs no comma at all?
choices: I like cats and dogs.
I like cats dogs and rabbits.
I like cats rabbits mice and dogs.
pool.hint: Commas start when a list has three or more items.
pool.explain: Cats and dogs is a list of two, so "and" is enough. The other two lists need commas.

pool.prompt: Where is the slip? Sam, Priya, Leo and, Max ran.
choices: The comma after "and"
The comma after "Sam"
The comma after "Priya"
pool.hint: "And" already joins the last two names. Does it need a comma after it?
pool.explain: No comma goes straight after "and". Sam, Priya, Leo and Max ran.

pool.prompt: Where is the slip? Red, blue and green, are my best colours.
choices: The comma after "green"
The comma after "Red"
There is no slip
pool.hint: Green is the last item. Is the list still going?
pool.explain: No comma after the last item. The list is over, and the verb "are" follows straight on.

pool.prompt: Why do we put commas in a list?
choices: To show where each item ends
To show which word is most important
To fill the space between words
pool.hint: Think about the reader in the lab. What changed in the panel when you added a comma?
pool.explain: List commas separate the items, so the reader can tell where one thing ends and the next begins.

choices: Do you want tea, coffee or juice?
Do you want, tea coffee or juice?
Do you want tea coffee, or, juice?
pool.hint: Lists can end with "or" as well as "and". The commas work the same way.
pool.explain: Tea, coffee or juice: a comma after tea, then "or" before the last choice.

pool.prompt: Without the serial comma, how many commas does a list of {n} names need?
pool.hint: Count a comma after each name, but not after the last two, which "and" joins.
pool.explain: A list of {n} names needs {=n-2} commas when there is no comma before "and".

pool.prompt: Ella wrote: I bought, bread, jam and butter. What should she change?
choices: Take out the comma after "bought"
Add a comma after "jam" and take out every other comma
Take out the comma after "bread"
pool.hint: The list starts with the first item. Is "bought" part of the list?
pool.explain: No comma before the first item: I bought bread, jam and butter. The comma after bread is needed.

pool.prompt: Which sentence uses the serial (Oxford) comma?
choices: I saw lions, tigers, and bears.
I saw lions, tigers and bears.
I saw lions tigers and bears.
pool.hint: The serial comma is the one just before the final "and".
pool.explain: Lions, tigers, and bears has a comma before "and": the serial comma. Lions, tigers and bears is also correct without it.

pool.prompt: A list of {n} things has no serial comma. You add one more thing to the list. How many commas does the new list need?
pool.hint: The new list has {n} + 1 items. Without the serial comma, it needs two fewer commas than items.
pool.explain: The new list has {=n+1} items, so it needs {=n+1} − 2 = {=n-1} commas.
